Plug in the values of a, b, and c. Calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac) to see if there are real solutions. If it’s positive, you get two real roots; if zero, one; if negative, no real solutions. To find stationary points, first take the derivative of y with respect to x, which gives you f'(x). Then, set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are the candidates for stationary points. Plug each back into the original equation to find the corresponding y-values. Finally, classify each point as a maximum, minimum, or point of inflection using the second derivative test. This helps understand where the function changes direction.
